newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Buyback speculation spurs CSR shares on.
newsitem.headline: Buyback speculation spurs CSR shares on.

text.p: Shares in building materials, sugar and aluminium group CSR Ltd bucked the bearish Australian stock market trend on Tuesday with a 1.7 percent jump to A$5.25 on speculation it would introduce a share buyback programme.
Today's level equals the 3-1/2 year high reached in mid-June and comes amid a broader market pullback of about 1.6 percent as resource stocks softened with a battered bullion price.
"CSR have been particularly strong on ongoing rumours about a buyback," said David Iron, head of institutional sales at HSBC Jame Capel.
The company, which has been under pressure to improve its earnings, reported a 36 percent fall in net profit to A$212 million for the 12 months to March 31, 1997.
However, the company said it expected better results in the current year with a modest recovery in Australian building and construction activity and healthy levels of activity in U.S. markets.
CSR declined to comment on the market speculation.
CSR shares closed eight cents higher at A$5.24 on solid turnover of 2.8 million shares.
